description.narrative: The main project objective is to build the confidence and skills of persons with disabilities living with HIV and affected by tuberculosis to standup to stigma they experience in social (health and education) Service delivery in two subcounties of Nyendo-Mukungwe and Kyesiiga of Masaka city/district. Although data about HIV/AIDS prevalence among people with disabilities is scarce, UNAIDS2017 report on disability and HIV/AIDS noted that Data from sub-Saharan Africa suggest an increased risk of HIV infection of 1.48 times in men with disabilities and 2.21 times in women with disabilities compared with men without disabilities. The report further asserts that People with disabilities are found in all key and vulnerable populations, including sexworkers; lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender people; children out of school; people experiencing violence; women and girls and adolescents; Yet, people withdisabilities, in particular women and girls experience discrimination in HIV/AIDS service delivery and they may be turned away from sexual, reproductive and HIV services Or may be considered a low priority (Abimanyi J. ET’AL. (2017) The envisaged change of this project is a strong network of Peer Support Groups of People with Disabilities Living with HIV/AIDS through which disabled self-advocates living with HIV/AIDS and affected by tuberculosis together with their caregivers confidently engage with policy- makers and implementers at local government and service delivery levelurging them to implement international commitments, national and local legislative/ policy provisions promoting disability inclusion and non-discrimination in HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and other health services. There is evidence that Peer supportgroups of people living with HIV/AIDS and TB have performed criticaladvocacy roles for promoting inclusion of people with disabilities in national TB and HIV/AIDS responses which are usually designedwithout consideration of the unique needs of people experiencing double stigmatization. In keeping with the “nothing about us without us” philosophy, this project will support MADIPHA to expand and strengthen the network of peer support groups of people with disabilities living with HIV/AIDS and affected by tuberculosis. The solutions proposed by MADIPHA to bring about the envisaged change include 1) mentorship and coaching for disability inclusive HIV/AIDS service delivery champions to develop the confidence and skills for engaging with decisionmakers, 2) supporting the Masaka disabled Association of People with Disabilities Livingwith HIV/AIDS peer support group to develop strategic partnerships with mainstream civil society organizations promoting inclusive accessible HIV/AIDS andTBservices, 3) mentorship and coaching of elected leaders of people with disabilities on how to advocate for the implementation of disability inclusive policies and programs

participating-org.narrative:
MADIPHA is an association of Persons with disabilities who have tested positive for HIV or are affected by TB, together with their family members. The Association started its operations in 2009 in the districts of Masaka, Kalungu, Lwengo, Bukomansimbi, and Rakai.MADIPHA is arguably the first organized peer-support network of people with disabilities living with HIV/AIDS and people affected by TB in Uganda. The Association is in the process of scaling up its activities to include other districts outside its original districts of operations, and to organize other persons with disabilities living with and affected by HIV/AIDS and TB in these districts to advocate for their rights in all national HIV/AIDS and TB programs in Uganda. MADIPHA unites people with disabilities at the intersection of TB, HIV/AIDS, and disability in Uganda. MADIPHA links people with disabilities and their families to HIV/TB prevention, diagnosis, and treatment and care services. MADIPHA integrates the most marginalized people withhigh support needs into peer support groups to reduce stigma and discrimination. MADIPHA empowers the community of people with disabilities living with HIV and AIDS to participate in TB and HIV program design and delivery. MADIPHA spearheads advocacy forthe recognition of the rights of people living at the intersection of disability, TB and HIV to address healthcare, social and economic barriers. The BOD of MADIPHA is largely constituted from the membership of persons with disabilities living positively with HIV/AIDS and affected by TB who make the entire raft of governance decisions in the organization, with 60% are women and there must be a youth. Further a number of gender responsive policies were developed including; Child Protection, Prevention ofSexual Abuse, Exploitation and Harassment and Safe Guarding.
1. In2021, MADIPHA’s ongoing advocacy for inclusion of disability in the design of local TB/HIV programming resulted in the formulation and passage of 7 pieces of local legislations for promoting disability inclusive HIV/AIDS and TB prevention and control in form of a District Ordinance for Rakai District and 6 bi-laws for Kyesiga Sub County, Lukaya Town Council, Malongo Sub County, Kiseka sub county, Lwengo Town Council and Kitanda Sub County, based on MADIPHA’s 21 Recommendations for disability-inclusive TB and HIV programs.
2. Since 2019 MADIPHA has trained over 50 health workers in five districts on how to attend to people with disabilities. In Greater Masaka, MADIPHA has founded fivedistrict association of people with disabilities living with HIV and affected by Tuberculosis supporting up to 500 members. Our advocacy seeks for empowerment to expand similar policies at the local, national and international levels. 3. And Buildingourorganizational structures, governance and management systems to strengthen the capacity to carry out advocacy on the rights of persons with disabilities living with HIV<(>&<)>AIDS and affected by Tuberculosis in the region.
MADIPHA is avery unique organization bringing together persons with disabilities who are boldly living positively with HIV/AIDS and affected by Tuberculosis (TB). Members of MADIPHA have in many ways overcome the double stigma of disability and HIV/AIDS and TB and are therefore a living testimony for the kind of change the organization is advocating.
Apart from the respective local government departments, disability leadership structures, HIV and TB service centres/organization which are critical for referral purposes, MADIPHA established a strong working relationship with the local cultural Institution (Buddu) of Buganda Kingdom sealed with an MOU to promote the rights of person with disability in the area. The local Chief (Pokino) is the champion for promoting disability rights.

comment.narrative:
With or without MADIPHA, the rightsholders are able to meet and discuss issues that affect them, and how to confront them through various strategies. They are reaching out to more peers indicating a project multiplier effect in their jurisdiction.
Group members through their leaders negotiated partnerships with other organisations to amplify their voices and be a foundation for inclusion and inclusive practices. Each group was supported to legalise operation thus forming a basis upon which they, through meetings, are able to raise discuss and binding concerns.

comment.narrative: For the project to have better manageable interventions and to maximise impact more efficiently, MADIPHA narrowed down rightsholder groups to 3 with a membership of 45 members per group, reaching out to 145 individual members. In their groups: • Been empowered to hold advocacy meetings with powerholders that yielded results such as access to livelihood programs by government. Through a petition to Masaka City Council, copied to relevant officials, rightsholders demanded the inclusion of accessibility standards in the design and construction of public infrastructure, with a focus on the ongoing reconstruction of Masaka Recreation Stadium.

comment.narrative: Of the 145 Rightsholders reached by the project, 25 peers identified as Disability-inclusive advocacy champions for disability-inclusive HIV, TB and other social services delivery in Masaka. The rightsholders in there groups are able to speak in public, an indicator of higher self-esteem. They are able to confidently engage duty bearers.
